microwave-and-optical-communications--cu.title: cutoff from the transverse wavenumber
microwave-and-optical-communications--cu.note: Below f_c the axial β turns imaginary and the mode evanesces; above it β is real and sets the guide wavelength.

microwave-and-optical-communications--do.title: low-order rectangular waveguide modes
microwave-and-optical-communications--do.note: A TM mode needs both indices non-zero, so TM11 is the lowest TM mode; a > b is what makes TE10 the dominant mode.

microwave-and-optical-communications--ma.title: E-plane, H-plane and magic tees
rows: arm 3 sees nothing from the H arm
arm 3 sees nothing from the E arm
both arms split 3 dB, 180° between them
E and H arms isolated, S34 = 0
microwave-and-optical-communications--ma.note: Merging the two tees gives equal 3 dB splits with a 180° difference between the collinear arms, while the E and H arms stay isolated.

microwave-and-optical-communications--ci.title: three-port circulator

steps.label: forward wave in at port 1 leaves at port 2
wave in at port 2 leaves at port 3
wave in at port 3 leaves at port 1

microwave-and-optical-communications--ci.note: The ferrite bias fixes one rotation sense, so the reverse direction 2 to 1 is refused and is absorbed by a matched load instead.

microwave-and-optical-communications--at.title: optical power budget in decibels
symbols: power into and out of the span
microwave-and-optical-communications--at.note: In dB every element of the span simply adds, so a link is budgeted by subtraction instead of by multiplying factors.

microwave-and-optical-communications--nu.title: acceptance cone from total internal reflection
symbols: index outside the fibre, 1 in air
critical angle at the core-cladding boundary
microwave-and-optical-communications--nu.note: A large NA gathers more light but supports more modes, so single-mode fibre keeps both NA and core diameter small.

microwave-and-optical-communications--si.title: step-index, graded-index and single-mode fibre
microwave-and-optical-communications--si.note: Grading bends rays back continuously and cuts modal dispersion; reducing to one mode removes it and leaves only chromatic dispersion.

microwave-and-optical-communications--di.title: pulse spread and the bit-rate limit
microwave-and-optical-communications--di.note: Modal spread falls with NA², which is why a small-NA graded core reaches gigahertz per kilometre while a step-index core stops at tens of megahertz.
